profile.headline: Software Engineering Leader @ Pinterest | Capacity and Efficiency
profile.summary:
Anchoring system performance initiatives at Pinterest, my role as a Software Engineer centers on cloud cost efficiency and software development. Our efforts in migrating workloads to AWS Graviton instances have achieved performance boosts and significant cost reductions.

Leadership in mentoring and performance analysis has been pivotal; steering a team that develops tools for profiling at cloud scale, we contribute to Pinterest's robust software ecosystem. My background in computer architecture research complements our mission to optimize large-scale computing systems.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer - Capacity Engineering
positions.description:
* Served as Capacity Lead, ensuring robust capacity allocation, delivering efficient and robust capacity to mitigate external risk.
* Led the Graviton Migration project, achieving $30M in savings and migrating 25% of the fleet to Arm-based Graviton instance offerings.
* Spearheaded Capacity Automation initiatives, including building capacity tooling and automating capacity management.
* Mentored junior engineers and contractors, contributing to the development of key capacity tooling.

positions.title: Staff Performance Engineer
positions.description:
• Team lead for programming language, runtimes, and libraries performance analysis and optimization
• Manage team by fostering grown and setting technical direction for four engineers
• Evaluate and understand performance implications of runtime mechanism including garbage collection, intrinsics, and code generation
• Experienced in planning and executing team projects with strong communication with customers and management
• Develop software and perform performance analysis to optimize software for existing and upcoming Arm servers
• Develop benchmarks to stress architecture features and perform competitive analysis
• Lead technical collaboration with key datacenter partners with focus on providing expertise and open lines of communication

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Thesis Title: "Application-Level Modeling and Analysis of Time and Energy for Optimizing Power-Constrained Extreme-Scale Applications"

• Examined power-constrained runtime optimization of task graph-based high performance applications
• Constructed eaudit tool for exploring parallel application energy consumption on CPUs and accelerators
• Built Eiger Statistical Modeling Framework for fast, approximate models of performance for modeling large scale systems

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Supported the graduate-level Advanced Programming Techniques course, covering advanced C++, OpenGL, CUDA, MPI, and OpenMP programming.

positions.title: Student Intern
positions.description:
• Created methodology for instrumenting application behavior to drive architecture-independent models of cache behavior
• Produced a robust model of cache behavior that delays selection of configuration until after runtime instrumentation

positions.title: Student Intern
positions.description:
• Explored feasibility of dynamic frequency scaling to optimize performance of HPC systems under power cap
• Implemented measurement and modeling infrastructure for large-scale power data collection on cluster test bed

positions.title: Student Intern
positions.description:
• Interfaced Eiger with the SST/macro macro-scale simulator
• Explored machine learning techniques for regression and dimensionality reduction and their application to model generation

positions.title: Student Intern
positions.description:
• Developed buffered flow-control mechanism for exascale supercomputer network simulation
• Analyzed contention effects on buffer capacity in large scale computer networks

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Worked on GPU VSIPL, an implementation of the Vector Signal Image Processing Library for the NVIDIA CUDA platform
• Implemented blocked SVD algorithm on GPU accelerator

publications.title: Application Modeling for Scalable Simulation of Massively Parallel Systems
publications.publisher: IEEE International Conference on High Performance Computing and Communications (HPCC) · Aug 1, 2015

publications.title: Understanding Performance--Energy Tradeoffs: When is Energy Not Time?
publications.publisher: Workshop on Modeling & Simulation of Systems and Applications (MODSIM) · Aug 1, 2015
